clue.text: Divvying a very quiet beginning, otherwise turning into this with a gin sling.

indicators.note: says that the a and the very quiet piece come first, at the start of the answer

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
'or' means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll be late'

indicators.note: the word into is turned about, its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: to sling is to throw about, so the letters of gin are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sharing out drinks starts very quietly, then switches to gin slings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' puts A and PP (very quiet) first, then OR; 'turning' makes TION from INTO, and 'sling' tosses GIN into ING. 'Gin sling' is really a cocktail, which hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To apportion is to share out in portions, so divvying up is the same act of distribution.

clue.text: Color in the top of your head, putting the time ahead.

definitions.note: a participle phrase for the verb: to predate a document is to put an earlier date on it

indicators.note: the colour word is placed in the middle of the word for the top of the head

parts.note: the pate is the crown of the head
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Someone dyes their crown and moves the clock forward at the same time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' tells you to put the colour inside the pate. 'Ahead' here means earlier: a predated cheque carries a date ahead of, that is before, the true one.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate is to give something an earlier date than the actual one, setting its time before the real event.

clue.text: When you run in it, you might have to jump things.

definitions.text: When you run in it, you might have to jump things.

parts.words: When you run in it, you might have to jump things.
parts.note: a plain description of a running contest with barriers, ladders and nets to get over

explanation.walkthrough: The clue simply describes the event; the second word of the answer sits in the across light that says 'See 3 down'.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle race is a running contest in which competitors must climb, crawl or leap over barriers along the course.

clue.text: Members of a certain order, where a well-known musical family takes their chairs, when slightly disturbed.

parts.note: the von Trapp family singers, of The Sound of Music

indicators.note: the word for sitting is mildly jumbled, its letters reshuffled

parts.note: someone who takes a chair sits

explanation.surface: A famous singing family settles into seats belonging to some religious order, causing a bit of a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: The family is the von Trapps of The Sound of Music, and 'slightly disturbed' stirs what people taking chairs do into ISTS. Fittingly, the order is the monastic one famous for keeping silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Trappists are Cistercian monks of the Strict Observance, a Catholic religious order.

clue.text: In Sappho, per antiquarians, one can find an elaborate musical drama.

indicators.note: the answer is sitting in the words that follow, across the gap between them
says the answer can be found within the text rather than built

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Sappho, all of per and the start of antiquarians

explanation.surface: Scholars of antiquity uncover a lavish stage work in the poems of Sappho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'one can find' both say the answer is sitting inside the text: sappHO PER Antiquarians.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music throughout, typically with orchestra, singers and elaborate production.

clue.text: Came out, but gets called into court.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emerged or was published
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into IS SUED, which is what happens to someone called into court by a plaintiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issued has been put out or emerged, as a newspaper is issued each morning.

clue.text: One of the Windward islands, not quite great, and absolutely nothing to the Spanish.

indicators.note: the word great is cut short, losing its last letters

parts.note: taken as written, then cut short
nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island is described as not quite great and worth nothing at all to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts GREAT back to GRE, and NADA is Spanish for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is the southernmost island of the Windward chain in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Proceed diligently, as testators sometimes have to do.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to set about a job energetically and wholeheartedly

definitions.text: as testators sometimes have to do
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a testator is someone who makes a will, and must sometimes deal with that document

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'with a will' means eagerly; read literally, it has the testator handling the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: To work with a will is an idiom for labouring energetically and with determination.

clue.text: Not in the required fashion.

parts.note: 'required' stands for necessary, so the phrase describes doing something in a way that was not needed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like clothes, but it means manner here: a manner that is not required.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnecessarily means in a way that is not needed, describing an action done without requirement.

clue.text: The main description would be nothing to write about, with a couple of points to end everything.

indicators.note: says the a goes at the very end of the answer

parts.note: O is the zero shape, nothing
to pen is to write
S and E, two compass points

explanation.surface: A dull seascape: nothing worth writing about, plus a few final points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To end everything' sends the A to the very end, after the two points. 'The main' is the old poetic word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main, so the definition is a phrase describing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea is ocean away from land, the expanse that poets call the main.

clue.text: Oriental makes a point, with a harsh word.

parts.note: E is a compass point, east
stern is a word meaning harsh

explanation.surface: A man from the Orient makes his point with a sharp reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern are synonyms, both describing things from Asia or the East.

clue.text: Cuddly thing with a possibly strange appetite is a knock-out according to the description.

definitions.text: Cuddly thing with a possibly strange appetite

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
a la, borrowed from French, means in the manner of, after the description of

explanation.surface: A cute creature with odd eating habits turns out to be a stunner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'possibly strange appetite' is the animal's diet of nothing but eucalyptus leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a furry Australian marsupial that looks like a teddy bear and lives on eucalyptus leaves.

clue.text: In San Francisco or Salt Lake City, what you may do on a shingle.

definitions.text: In San Francisco or Salt Lake City
definitions.meaning: first meaning: what each of these is, the name of a place

definitions.text: what you may do on a shingle
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a shingle is a small signboard, and you place a name on it

explanation.walkthrough: A shingle here is the small sign a doctor or lawyer hangs out, not a roof tile or a pebble beach.
explanation.definitionFit: San Francisco and Salt Lake City are both examples of a toponym, the name given to a town or locality.

clue.text: On which you might write down your thoughts, I see by the sound of it–which is rather noble!

parts.words: On which you might write down your thoughts
parts.note: an idea list, a list on which ideas are jotted

indicators.note: the words I see, spoken, are heard as two letter names

parts.note: said aloud, I see sounds like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: A diarist notes their thoughts and exclaims about how high-minded it all sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA LIST is a list of thoughts; 'by the sound of it' turns the spoken 'I see' into the letters IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone idealistic holds lofty principles, which can be called noble in spirit.

clue.text: A brave nomenclature for what the tot might consider a choo-choo.

definitions.text: A brave nomenclature for what the tot might consider a choo-choo.

parts.words: A brave nomenclature for what the tot might consider a choo-choo.
parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and a choo-choo is a child's word for a train; the clue asks what such a warrior called the locomotive

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun here, not an adjective: the clue asks for the name a Native American warrior was said to give the steam train.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse is a nineteenth-century nickname for the steam locomotive, attributed in Westerns to Native Americans.

clue.text: See 3 down
The first word of 28 precedes this on certain occasions, with the following given to you.

definitions.text: The first word of 28 precedes this on certain occasions, with the following given to you.

parts.words: The first word of 28 precedes this on certain occasions, with the following given to you.
parts.note: the first word of 28 across is happy, and the song sung on these occasions continues 'to you'

explanation.walkthrough: 28 across begins HAPPY, and 'given to you' completes the song: Happy Birthday to You.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday is the yearly anniversary of a birth, celebrated with the familiar song of good wishes.

clue.text: Keep on talking and talking about what is a plaything for an angel.

definitions.text: Keep on talking and talking about
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... on a subject is to dwell on it tediously
second meaning: the stringed instrument angels are pictured playing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plaything' looks like a toy, but here it is a thing one plays music on.
explanation.definitionFit: To harp on is to keep returning to one topic, and the instrument is the traditional heavenly accompaniment.

clue.text: Somewhat scarlet, but beets might represent such on the table.

definitions.text: beets might represent such on the table
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into RED DISH, a crimson plate of beets.
explanation.definitionFit: Reddish describes a colour leaning toward red without being fully so, as scarlet partly is.

clue.text: Hangs around with, and forms part of the group of partners.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, keeps company with
second meaning: a plural noun, colleagues or partners in a business

explanation.walkthrough: The verb is said with a final 'ates' as in 'skates'; the noun usually ends in 'its', but both share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate is to mix socially, and associates are business partners or colleagues.

clue.text: Possibly a topic a cook might dish out.

definitions.note: a relative phrase for the noun: what a cook might serve

indicators.note: the letters might possibly form another word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook ladles out something, perhaps a subject for conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges 'a topic a', both little words included, to give the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy pudding made from cassava, a classic dish served from the kitchen.

clue.text: Admits being the way down supper, in part.

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words down supper, sitting across their gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of down and the start of supper

explanation.surface: Someone confesses as they head downstairs to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' says the answer is part of the text: dOWN SUPper. 'The way down' also hints that it reads downwards, as a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess or acknowledge a fault, the same as admitting it.

clue.text: It has a middling association with Longfellow, having lots of money to throw around like crazy!

definitions.text: It has a middling association with Longfellow

parts.words: lots of money to throw around like crazy
parts.note: wads are thick rolls of banknotes, the cash a big spender flashes
worth can mean having wealth to the value of, as in 'he is worth millions'

explanation.surface: A tall chap seems linked to someone with piles of cash to splash about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middling' points to a middle name: the poet was Henry Wadsworth Longfellow. 'Longfellow' tempts as a tall man, but it is the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadsworth is the middle name of the American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.

clue.text: Overoxidized, but if you are, you'll have to bone up!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: corroded by iron oxide

definitions.text: if you are, you'll have to bone up
definitions.meaning: second meaning: out of practice, needing to study again

explanation.walkthrough: To bone up is American slang for studying hard, which a rusty skill calls for.
explanation.definitionFit: Rusty describes iron coated with corrosion and, figuratively, skills weakened by lack of practice.

clue.text: One who overindulges, sort of like Perot.

indicators.note: a sort of Perot is a rough version of the name, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker is compared to the Texan billionaire Ross Perot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges the name; Ross Perot was a US presidential candidate in 1992 and 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is a habitual heavy drinker, someone given to excess with alcohol.

clue.text: It's French law to introduce a sibling briefly when you have infestation with the parasitic eyeworm.

parts.note: loi is the French word for law
sis is the short form of sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A French legal tangle is blamed on a sister and an eye parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: Loiasis is the tropical disease caused by the Loa loa worm, which can crawl across the eye.

clue.text: Breed of cattle taken as part of the Communist questioning.

parts.note: a red is a Communist
a poll is a questioning of people for their opinions

explanation.surface: Livestock is swept up in a Communist interrogation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Poll is a hornless red-coated British cattle breed kept for beef and milk.

clue.text: One might hear it said on the first day.

definitions.text: One might hear it said on the first day.

parts.words: One might hear it said on the first day.
parts.note: the first day of the year, January 1, is when this greeting is exchanged

explanation.walkthrough: 'The first day' means the first day of the year, not of a week or a job.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the greeting people exchange on January 1, wishing each other well for the coming twelve months.
